mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature notarized in origin country then Consular Legalization at Egyptian Embassy or Consulate

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, officers and ultimate beneficial owners must be screened against the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) watchlists, Egyptian Central Bank sanctions lists, United Nations Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, HMG HM Treasury consolidated list, and the European Union financial sanctions database prior to incorporation and on an ongoing basis. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for all non-resident natural persons and entities owing to the medium-risk maritime bunkering and fuel supply profile. Any PEP or sanctioned-name match triggers immediate Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) filing and postponement of incorporation approval.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Electronic Incorporation and Name Reservation System (www.gafi.gov.eg / Inves't Egypt platform) operated jointly with the Commercial Registry of the Ministry of Trade and Industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The approved commercial/company name must be written in Arabic for the primary statutory name. A Latin transliteration/English equivalent may be registered as a secondary auxiliary name, provided it is an exact phonetic transliteration of the Arabic name and does not duplicate any previously reserved name. Names using Islamic religious expressions or specific holy words are only permitted with prior ministerial authorization.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal through the GAFI electronic portal or at the GAFI headquarters in Cairo within thirty calendar days of the rejection notice. The appeal must state factual distinctiveness, explain the absence of likelihood of confusion, and, where a ministerial approval is required, attach the relevant pre-clearance letter. The Name Clearance Committee shall issue a decision within fifteen working days. If rejected, a further appeal may be brought before the GAFI Juridical Affairs Committee with a final deadline of fifteen days from the first appeal decision. A fresh name reservation application may be filed concurrently for a second proposed name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for marine bunkering and fuel replenishment activities. The Egyptian General Authority for Investment requires a physical registered office in Egypt capable of housing original corporate records, meeting minutes, UBO files, and acting as a valid address for service of process. A virtual office may be used only as a supplementary correspondence address and must never be the sole registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. Regulated marine fuel bunkering exposes the entity to unannounced physical inspections under maritime and customs supervision by the Egyptian Maritime Transport Sector, the Administrative Control Authority, and the Ministry of Supply; estimated 75% probability of an on-site inspection within the first 18 months of licensing and annual reinspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended, Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, and corresponding Executive Regulations; provisions governing limited liability companies under Articles 102-117 of the Companies Law and GAFI implementing rules
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registry and Investor Services Center, Ministry of Trade and Industry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Contract (Aqd at-Ta'sis) and Articles of Association (Statute) submitted through the GAFI electronic incorporation application
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a limited liability company under Law No. 159/1981; the entire subscribed capital must be deposited in an Egyptian bank and covered by a bank certificate as a condition precedent to registration; foreign currency subscriptions are held in an Egyptian escrow bank account pending registration
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that all incorporators and founding shareholders hereby confirm the full subscription of the share capital according to the annexed Establishment Contract and ratify the Articles of Association as presented. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office shall be at the address stated in the Establishment Contract and all statutory notifications shall be filed therewith. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed General Manager and [Name] is appointed Secretary/Director, with full authority to represent the company and to execute filings with GAFI, the tax authority, the commercial registry, banks, and licensing authorities. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the authorized representatives are empowered to open corporate bank accounts and to sign the standard license application for marine bunkering operation permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Name Reservation and Legal Form Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Center and Egyptian Commercial Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request via the GAFI online portal or in person, selecting 'Limited Liability Company' as the legal form. The proposed name must not be identical, confusingly similar, or contrary to public order. The applicant pays the name reservation fee and receives a provisional name approval certificate valid for up to one year.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copies of the founding shareholders
Signed memorandum of intent identifying the proposed legal form
Proof of payment of the name clearance fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an administrative appeal to the GAFI Name Committee within 15 days accompanied by alternative name options; the committee must issue a reasoned decision within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Establishment Contract and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian Notary Public and GAFI Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a licensed legal advisor to prepare the Arabic-language Company Establishment Contract and Articles of Association. All shareholders or their legal proxies must sign the contract before a licensed notary, and notarization verifies identity, capacity, and consent. The notarized instrument is then submitted to GAFI for a preliminary compliance review.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney notarized and legalized if signed by foreign shareholders
Shareholders' identification documents and tax identification numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI returns the documents for correction, rectify the indicated clauses and resubmit within 15 days; a formal objection may be lodged with the GAFI Legal Affairs Department if the objections exceed the statutory basis.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Bank Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate bank account in the name of the company under formation or deposit the entire subscribed capital into an escrow account held by one of the founding shareholders. The bank verifies the capital amount, issues a certificate of capital deposit, and blocks the funds until the company is registered. Upon registration, the blocked amount becomes the company's opening paid-up capital.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application and declaration of source of funds
Proof of payment of capital subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the certificate due to incomplete documentation, complete the bank's KYC requirements; if the refusal is arbitrary, submit a complaint to the Central Bank of Egypt Customer Protection Unit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Application and Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarized incorporation contract, articles of association, bank capital certificate, and all supporting documents to the GAFI digital platform or deliver the physical dossier to the GAFI One-Stop Shop. Pay the prescribed incorporation fees and obtain the GAFI incorporation approval that assigns the commercial registration eligibility.
required_dossiers: Lease contract or proof of title for the registered office address
Tax clearance or proof of submission of the founders' previous tax returns
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI queries the application, address all comments in writing through the One-Stop Shop and resubmit within 20 days; an administrative recourse before the GAFI Dispute Resolution Committee is available for wrongful rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration and Tax Card Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry Commercial Registry Office and Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After GAFI approval, file the incorporation contract with the local Commercial Registry office to obtain the commercial registration number. Concurrently, apply to the Egyptian Tax Authority for a tax card, tax registration number, and VAT certificate. These documents are required for bank account activation and subsequent operational licenses.
required_dossiers: Notarized Establishment Contract and Articles of Association
General Manager and Directors' ID copies
Proof of payment of commercial registration and tax card fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry or ETA objects to the filing, correct any discrepancies in address or legal representation and resubmit within 10 days; an escalation to the district manager of the Commercial Registry or the ETA Client Assistance Unit is available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Seal, Bank Operation, and Post-Incorporation Governance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI, local commercial bank, and company founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Order the company seal from a licensed supplier, open or convert the temporary bank account into an operational corporate account, and execute the first board resolution in writing. Maintain the statutory register of members and meeting minutes at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Bank account operation sheet and required signatories documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays account activation, provide the complete corporate package and the Central Bank AML forms; if the delay exceeds ten working days, lodge a complaint with the bank's compliance officer and, if necessary, the Central Bank Banking Ombudsman.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources - Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC), Fuel Supply and Operations Directorate
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Marine Fuel Bunkering and Supply License (Marine Bunkering Operations Permit) issued by EGPC for ship refueling and lubricant replenishment services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Environmental Impact Assessment Registration with mandatory Environmental Inspection Report due to petroleum bunkering activities near navigation and coastal zones
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Egyptian Environmental Law No. 4 of 1994 as amended and Executive Regulations; oily-water effluent cannot exceed 15 ppm oil content before discharge, VOC emissions must be controlled to measurable levels under approved monitoring protocols, and waste handling must follow hazardous waste transfer manifests with final disposal at an eligible treatment facility; MARPOL 73/78 discharge requirements are imposed as a concession condition

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the General Administration of Civil Defense at the Ministry of Interior covering fuel storage areas, bunkering docks, firefighting equipment, evacuation routes, and explosion-proof installation; structural load inspection by a licensed engineer verifying the waterfront facility's berth and barge mooring capacity; workplace occupational health clearance from the Ministry of Manpower covering forklift operation, hazardous chemical handling, PPE use, and medical fitness of marine staff

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), the unified national tax agency (merging the former Income Tax, Sales Tax/VAT and Stamp Tax authorities); official e-portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; mandatory e-invoicing/e-receipt platform: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg with ETA REST API clearance endpoints for real-time fiscal stamping.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned Egyptian LLC registration procedure: (1) incorporate via the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) one-stop shop to obtain commercial register certificate and the statutory marine bunkering activity license; (2) file Tax Registration Application Form with ETA's central or local registration department within 30 days after commercial registration, attaching the certified memorandum of association, commercial register extract, GAFI license, board resolution, power of attorney and foreign parent details; (3) obtain a single unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) that simultaneously covers Corporate Income Tax, VAT, withholding and stamp tax accounts; (4) on the same TIN, complete mandatory VAT registration where annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000, or voluntary VAT registration where annual supplies exceed EGP 150,000 under VAT Law 67 of 2016 and its Executive Regulations; (5) onboard to ETA's e-invoicing/e-receipt API using an ETA-issued digital certificate, test environment validation, and production clearance credentials before the first taxable bunker supply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt has no US-style check-the-box regime; legal form governs classification, and an LLC is a resident juridical person subject to entity-level taxation on worldwide income. Statutory elections available under Law 91 of 2005 include: depreciation and capital-allowance method elections; SME simplified substantive tax regime election for turnover thresholds under Egypt's 2023 unified tax package; Investment Law 72 of 2017 tax-incentive elections for Suez Canal Economic Zone and eligible export-oriented activities; deemed-expense ratio elections for limited-cost logistics and export service providers; and group consolidation is not permitted. Hybrid mismatch exposure is addressed through MLI-aligned substance-over-form rules, controlled-foreign-company provisions, and transfer-pricing documentation rather than elective classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable supplies triggering mandatory VAT registration; voluntary registration available where annual taxable value exceeds EGP 150,000 (VAT Law 67 of 2016 and Executive Regulations; zero-rated export supplies may be excluded from the general threshold in prescribed circumstances).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing: all B2B tax invoices must be transmitted via ETA REST API in standard JSON/XML schema and digitally cleared or stamped by ETA before issuance to the buyer; uncleared invoices are fiscally invalid and deny input VAT recovery. B2C e-receipts, applicable to retail bunkering and ancillary marine-store sales, must be posted to ETA immediately after the point of sale with an ETA-generated fiscal QR code. Marine bunkering operators must integrate the ETA digital-signing engine with ERP, terminal-weighbridge, bunker-delivery and metering systems, retain ETA receipt tokens and QR stamps in the statutory archive, and align their invoice clearing flow with customs export declarations under NAFIZA.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Article 30 of VAT Law 67 of 2016 applies to exported goods that physically depart Egypt and to services rendered to non-residents for direct use in international trade or transport. Marine bunker fuel and lubricants delivered to a vessel bound on a foreign voyage qualify as zero-rated export sales where the supply originates from bonded or customs-approved storage, title passes to a non-resident ship owner or operator, the vessel clears Egyptian territorial waters on an international route, and the export declaration is validated by Egyptian Customs. The bunkering service component may also be zero-rated where the recipient is a non-resident carrier and the benefit is consumed outside Egypt. Documentation must be retained for at least five years; excess input VAT refund claims must comply with ETA procedural deadlines and reconciliation with e-invoice clearance data.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (single administrative document) released via Egypt's NAFIZA customs single window and stamped by Egyptian Customs for the specific bonded bunker lot
Bunker Delivery Note / quantity tally certified by the receiving vessel's master or chief engineer with port authority stamp
Bill of Lading, cargo manifest, or port clearance certificate evidencing the vessel's departure to a foreign destination on an international voyage
Sales contract and commercial invoice in freely convertible currency identifying the non-resident buyer and the vessel's IMO number
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an Egyptian licensed bank confirming receipt of export proceeds attributable to the matched bunker supply shipment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Egyptian Tax Authority compliance audits cross-match export declarations under NAFIZA, cleared e-invoice XML, port logs, bunker delivery tallies, and bank inward remittance records. Fraudulent or unsupported export zero-rating triggers: retrospective VAT clawback at the 14% standard rate on the contested supplies, disallowance of related input VAT credits on bunker fuel purchases, late-payment surcharges of not less than 2% per month of the assessed tax, administrative fines ranging from EGP 20,000 to EGP 1,000,000 under Article 75 of VAT Law 67 of 2016, and criminal imprisonment of up to five years for tax-evasion where fraudulent intent is established; responsible directors and managers may be held jointly liable for assessed arrears.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - Foreign Exchange Control Department and Banking Supervision & AML Sector
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The EGP is partially convertible. Current-account trade and shipping transactions, including marine fuel invoices issued to foreign-flagged vessels, are generally settled through CBE-authorised banks upon presentation of supporting documentation. Capital-account operations, including inbound equity contributions, shareholder loans, dividend remittances, and liquidation transfers, require an authorised Egyptian bank, CBE registration, and underlying corporate approval. Profit remittances are permitted only after audited financial statements, tax clearance, source-of-funds verification, and a valid inward-transfer certificate. USD-denominated bunkering revenue may be retained onshore in foreign-currency accounts, but conversion into EGP must take place at the prevailing authorised-bank market rate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Marine fuel export proceeds must be repatriated to Egypt through an authorised bank within 90 days of the bunker delivery receipt or bill of lading date, unless a documentary credit or ship-owner settlement schedule expressly approved by the bank provides another maturity. No fixed statutory conversion ratio is currently imposed under Egypt's liberalised exchange control regime; the exporter may retain up to 100% of USD proceeds in an onshore CBE-authorised foreign-currency account. Under temporary macro-prudential circulars, the CBE may require first-offer of export USD to the authorised bank, but conversion is at market rate and not by a fixed surrender percentage. Every export consignment must be supported by the bunker supply contract, the original BDN, the Egyptian customs manifest where applicable, the commercial invoice, and the bank's foreign-currency inflow certificate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD/EGP Operational Account and Designated Capital Escrow Sub-Account
EGP Current Account with USD Export-Proceeds Retention Account
Corporate Operational Account in EGP/USD with Trade Finance and Treasury Desk
Operational USD/EGP Account and Standby LC Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury custody and legally insufficient for capital escrow. Egyptian regulations require all in-country corporate capital, export proceeds, and operating collections to pass through a CBE-authorised bank. An offshore digital EMI is not recognised for Egyptian tax clearance, cannot issue an Egyptian IBAN, and cannot receive export-proceeds accreditation. The only feasible use is a supplementary collection rail for third-country bunkering payments, immediately forwarded by SWIFT MT103 to the Egyptian operating account; the full documentary trail must still be submitted to the Egyptian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Egyptian tier-1 banks generally require physical presence of at least one Egyptian-resident director, the UBO, or the appointed attorney-in-fact for the initial KYC interview. Remote video-only onboarding is normally declined for enhanced-risk bunkering entities. Non-resident shareholders must supply a notarised and apostilled power of attorney to an Egyptian financial manager. Original corporate documents, Arabic translation, commercial registration, tax card, import/export register, and CBE bank-account application are mandatory; electronic banking tokens are issued only after successful branch activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership structure with opaque ultimate beneficial ownership and no Egyptian tax representative
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled LLC memorandum and articles of association; UBO chart; passport copies of all shareholders; commercial registration, tax card, import/export license; parent-company bank reference; audited financials; local financial manager employment contract; notarised and apostilled power of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suez Canal or anchorage bunkering trade exposing the bank to sanctions risk from vessel, charterer, or cargo
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vessel IMO number; ship registry extract; ISM and ISPS certificates; AIS historical tracks covering the delivery window; charterparty or voyage order; bunker supply agreement; MARPOL-compliant BDN; OFAC, EU, UK OFSI, UN, and Egyptian sanctions-list screening results; valid bunkering licence from the Egyptian Maritime Transport Authority and Suez Canal Authority where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity USD wire receipts from multiple port-state banks without visible physical cargo delivery
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Egyptian e-invoice; commercial invoice; bill of lading or sea waybill; port-authority supply log; CBE foreign-currency inflow certificate; bank statements cross-referenced to the BDN; insurance certificate; vessel port-call data; enhanced due-diligence questionnaire completed by the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash or split-payment structures using third-party paying agents for bunker stems
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy prohibiting cash; paying-agent identity and KYC; CRS/FATCA declarations; SWIFT sender and correspondent bank details; reconciliation ledger linking each third-party payment to a specific BDN and vessel voyage; Egyptian anti-money-laundering law compliance declarations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder must remit capital via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 COV in USD/EUR to the receiving Egyptian bank's designated foreign-currency account for EG_LLC. The payment narrative must clearly state 'equity contribution to EG_LLC under Egyptian Investment Law No. 72 of 2017' and reference the Commercial Registry number, Tax ID, and CBE inward-transfer purpose code for foreign direct investment. The receiving bank issues an Inward Transfer Certificate, which is the foundation for CBE FDI registration and later dividend or liquidation repatriation. Funds must not be parked in an EGP account before the inward foreign-currency certificate is issued; conversion to EGP is executed only after the corporate account is fully active.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For marine fuel procurement from overseas suppliers, the company should use SWIFT MT103 for spot or open-account payments, Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit under UCP600 for high-value petroleum cargoes, and Standby Letters of Credit under ISP98 as performance/custom security for bunker credit. Domestic fuel purchases from Egyptian refineries and bunker traders should be settled in EGP through the CBE-operated EGIPS high-value payment system or the Instant Payment Network, while USD export proceeds may be applied directly to foreign suppliers without forced conversion. All disbursements must reference the CBE purpose code, invoice number, BDN number, and be reconciled to customs release within five business days.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore trade-backed FX forward contracts with an Egyptian authorised bank, supported by underlying export or import exposure
FX swaps and roll-over swaps between USD and EGP executed through an authorised bank and reported to the CBE
Cross-currency swaps for medium-term debt or equity exposure, subject to CBE macro-prudential notification
Commodity-based price hedge integrated into the bunker supply contract, without offshore non-deliverable forwards being used as an onshore settlement tool

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form No. 33) covering the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of the fiscal year end; for calendar-year entities, no later than 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly penalty of 1% of the tax due per month or fraction thereof for late filing, plus additional 1% monthly penalty for late payment of tax; continued non-compliance triggers enforced collection and criminal fines under Law 91/2005

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements approved by the shareholders' general assembly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general assembly must be held within 6 months of fiscal year end; audited financial statements must be filed with GAFI within 1 month of approval; for calendar-year companies, effectively by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines per GAFI implementing rules; repeated failure may trigger administrative strike-off from commercial registry and suspension of the LLC's undertaking

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all Egyptian LLCs regardless of size; at least one certified independent auditor must be appointed by the general assembly for each fiscal year
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), materially aligned with IFRS, as issued by the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO return is required; UBO information is filed with GAFI at incorporation and must be updated within 30 days of any change in ownership. Share transfers exceeding 25% of shares or voting rights must be notified to GAFI and trigger a UBO register refresh; the annual general assembly reviews the UBO register as part of annual closing procedures.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.0% (standard corporate income tax rate for commercial enterprises under Law No. 91 of 2005 as amended by Law No. 23 of 2023; banks and similar financial institutions are subject to a 27.0% rate for the 2023–2024 period; the reduced rate applies to tax years commencing on or after 1 January 2023).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 allows a deduction of 30%–80% of licensed capital expenditure from taxable income, determined by geographical zone (80% for Zone A, 70% for Zone B, 50% for Central Egypt, 40% for Zone C, 30% for Zone D), spread over a maximum of 5 years; the deduction is increased by 10% for labour-intensive and export-oriented projects. Licensed free-zone undertakings in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) and public free zones (Port Said, Alexandria, Suez) may obtain a corporate tax exemption or a 0% rate on bunkering and marine-fuel supply income when the ETA confirms the free-zone activity test; newly incorporated LLCs may also access the general 5-year loss-carryforward and accelerated depreciation on specialized marine-asset classes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Income Tax Return Form No. 10 (Corporate Return on Tax on Income) for legal persons (LLC), filed exclusively through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) 'Bayan Misr' national e-filing portal (https://www.taxe.gov.eg); the filing captures the audited financial statements, tax computation work-paper, Transfer Pricing Declaration Form No. 63, and, where applicable, the investment-incentive schedules under Law No. 72 of 2017.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Form No. 10) with quarterly advance-installment declarations; monthly VAT, payroll tax and WHT statements remain due independently.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form No. 10 is due within 4 months after the fiscal year-end (for a 31 December year-end: 30 April of the following year). Quarterly advance tax installments are due on the last day of the 3rd, 6th, 9th and 12th months of the tax year. The return must be signed by the legal representative (LLC manager) and the licensed tax/certified accountant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: legal name, tax card number, commercial registration number, address, and legal-form classification (LLC).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident with an Egyptian permanent establishment (PE) must insert the PE's Egyptian tax card, Egyptian bank account and authorized tax agent's details; no Egyptian tax card should be quoted for a non-resident without a PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period and accounting basis: start/end dates of the tax year and accrual basis confirmation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the Egyptian PE branch fiscal year with the parent's fiscal year if the head-office return is already filed; the ETA accepts a 12-month period but pro-rates the first period of a newly registered branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue: bunkering and double-fuel sales, marine lubricants, brokering commissions, demurrage, surveying and related supply-chain revenue from Suez Canal transits and commercial shipping.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Egyptian-source revenue attributable to the PE is reportable; integrate the PE with the head office through a documented branch income statement, but do not include fees billed directly by the foreign head office to Egyptian ports.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales: opening inventory, marine-fuel purchases, import duties, barging and lightering costs, storage-tank expenses, terminal throughput fees, and closing inventory reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must use arm's-length pricing for intercompany fuel purchases from the parent or related suppliers; the ETA will benchmark the cost base against Egyptian BDN (Bunker Delivery Note) and customs data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit reconciliation: comparison between operational bunker volumes (surveyor reports, BDN, quantity-meters) and accounted turnover; any unexplained quantity variance must be explained in the notes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjustments to internal consumption, vessel-to-vessel transfers and tax-free free-zone sales must be supported by the customs and Suez Canal Authority (SCA) statistics for the non-resident licensed operator.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses and deductions: port dues, towage, crew and salaries, bank charges, insurance, depreciation, professional fees and repair/maintenance of bunker barges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head-office overhead allocations are deductible only if supported by a cost-allocation study and Egyptian TP documentation; the ETA frequently disallows 100% of unsubstantiated management fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory add-backs and disallowed items: taxes and penalties paid, contributions above the statutory ceilings (donations: 4% of taxable profit; CSR spends: 8%), and non-verifiable cash purchases.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding tax borne by the Egyptian PE on behalf of a foreign licensor cannot be deducted as an expense and must be added back if mistakenly booked.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Investment incentives: deduction of 30%–80% of licensed capital assets under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, with the geographic-zone multiplier and the 5-year spread completed in the attached schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Free-zone and SCZone licensed bunkering assets are excluded from the capital-cost deduction to avoid double-dipping with the free-zone exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable-base computation and rate: accounting profit, adjusted by add-backs and exemptions, then applying 25.0% (or 27.0% for financial institutions) to determine the assessed corporate tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE's taxable profit is the same as an Egyptian resident branch; the head office's foreign taxes are not creditable unless a treaty protocol permits, so the PE should separately claim treaty-residence credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits and payments: deductible quarterly advance installments, amounts withheld at source, foreign tax credits under the applicable DTA, and the balance payable or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the DTA relief approval and the foreign tax authority's Tax Residency Certificate before claiming foreign tax credits; the refund route is initiated through the annual return with supporting TRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer Pricing Declaration (Form No. 63): arms-length identification of related parties, aggregate transaction values, method applied, and confirmation of the Local File / Master File thresholds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident owned LLC triggers Form No. 63 automatically whenever related-party transactions occur; the PE branch is treated as a separate taxpayer and must complete the same declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Distribution statement: declaration of dividends proposed to be distributed and the corresponding 10% profit-distribution withholding tax to be remitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The LLC must withhold 10% from dividends paid to the non-resident parent and declare the amounts in the monthly WHT statement; treaty-reduced rates require the ETA clearance described below.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form No. 10 attracts a lump-sum penalty of EGP 5,000 for ordinary taxpayers and up to EGP 20,000 for large taxpayers, while late payment of the assessed corporate tax adds a monthly surcharge of 2% of the outstanding amount (including for part of a month, effectively accreting day-by-day) plus interest at the Central Bank of Egypt credit rate; persistent non-filing enables the ETA to issue an administrative self-assessment, double the final amount, publish the taxpayer in the tax-default list, and impose a travel ban on the LLC managers.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10.0% (final Egyptian withholding tax on dividends distributed by an Egyptian-resident LLC to a non-resident shareholder, per Article 58 of Law No. 91 of 2005; no additional Egyptian 'secondary' tax is levied on the repatriation; distributions to Egyptian-resident corporate shareholders may be exempt under the participation regime when the participation threshold and holding period are satisfied).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must deliver to the Egyptian paying entity and to the ETA (i) an original or certified Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction, (ii) a Beneficial Ownership declaration confirming entitlement to the treaty rate, and (iii) a completed ETA treaty-relief application (Form No. 986 for DTA treatment) filed together with the distribution documents. The Egyptian payer applies the reduced treaty rate only after the ETA has acknowledged the clearance; if the full 10% is withheld, the beneficial owner applies to the ETA for a refund against the DTA certificate. Ratified MLI positions add the Principal Purpose Test (PPT), so an LLC whose sole purpose is treaty-shopping will be denied relief and the 10% (or higher default) WHT will be enforced.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties for the use of intellectual or industrial rights is 20% of the gross Egyptian-source amount; statutory withholding on debt interest is 20% of gross (10% for interest on bank deposit accounts). Under bilateral treaties the rates are commonly capped between 10% and 15% (e.g., the US-Egypt DTA applies 15% to interest and royalties, with dividends at 15% generally and 5% for a 10% corporate shareholder; the UK-Egypt DTA applies similar moderation), and the ETA requires the TRC plus beneficial-ownership documentation to substantiate every reduced rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory when the Egyptian taxpayer's aggregate related-party transactions reach EGP 10,000,000 per tax year (per ETA Decree No. 537 of 2019 and the Egyptian Transfer Pricing Guidelines); Master File: mandatory when the MNE group's worldwide consolidated revenue reaches EGP 200,000,000; Country-by-Country Report: mandatory for a constituent entity of a MNE group whose consolidated group revenue is at or above EGP 18,000,000,000. The annual Transfer Pricing Declaration (Form No. 63) is obligatory in every return regardless of values.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations as a separate statute, but substance-over-form is implemented through Article 44 of Law No. 91 of 2005 (the General Anti-Avoidance Rule), the 'place of effective management' test for tax residence, beneficial-ownership clauses in DTAs and the MLI Principal Purpose Test. An LLC that cannot demonstrate physical premises, licensed marine-bunkering operations, qualified personnel, tank/berth capacity and DTA-consistent decision-making may be recharacterized as a conduit or sham; free-zone exemption and treaty relief are thereby revoked retroactively with full tax, surcharges and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion: Under-declaration of Marine-Fuel Revenues
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of cash or Swift-wire bunkering sales, fabrication of Bunker Delivery Notes, use of fake supplier invoices for imported low-sulphur fuel, inflation of operating losses, or matching-pair Suez/Port Said/Petroleum-trade invoices designed to suppress taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 133 of Law No. 91 of 2005: imprisonment for not less than 6 months and not more than 5 years and a fine of EGP 10,000–50,000, together with confiscation of the evaded assets, payment of the full evaded tax plus the 2% monthly late-payment surcharge, and publication of the conviction; the ETA additionally imposes the investment-incentive claw-back for the year of the offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The LLC managers, financial officer and signatories are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax when the veil is pierced for fraud; the ETA applies civil asset freezes, travel bans and the blocking of personal bank accounts; criminal sentences disqualify directors from managing a company under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation: Margin Stripping and Sham Intercompany Invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The foreign parent re-invoices bunker fuel to the Egyptian LLC at inflated margins; the LLC pays 5–15% of turnover as 'management services' with no evidence of performance; intercompany loans receive above-market interest; or the Egyptian entity is left a riskless title-holder so that profit migrates to the low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA reallocates the profit to the Egyptian taxable base and assesses the 25.0% tax plus the monthly 2% delay surcharge; a mandatory fine of EGP 10,000–50,000 applies to the false Transfer Pricing Declaration; undocumented head-office charges are totally disallowed; the reallocation may extend back under the 5-year assessment window, with the full limitation period extended in fraud cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign Form No. 63 with false related-party values commit a false-statement offense carrying personal criminal liability; the ETA can seek civil restitution from directors and the tax agent; a travel ban and asset freeze are routinely issued when the amended assessment exceeds the LLC's ability to pay.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance in Marine Bunkering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC exists solely as an invoice mill: it has no offices, no licensed bunker barges or shore tanks, no crew or operational contracts, no board minutes, and decisions are taken by a non-resident principal; bunker volumes require physical supply assets in Egypt but the entity has none; the free-zone or SCZone exemption hides the true non-resident trader.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of Article 44 GAAR: the shell LLC is disregarded, the foreign principal is deemed to carry on a PE in Egypt, the free-zone/SCZone exemption is revoked retroactively, corporate tax is assessed on the imputed Egyptian-source profits with the 2% monthly surcharge, and the ETA cancels the LLC's tax card and VAT registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and incorporators are jointly liable for the tax shortfall and for false statements in the registration file; courts have ordered the personal confiscation of nominee assets and imposed travel bans; the Commercial Registry may strike the LLC while shareholders are barred from new registration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering: Trade-Based Money Laundering in Cash and LC Bunkering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Large cash and SWIFT payments for vessel refueling are layered through flag-of-convenience suppliers, Standby LCs obscure the beneficial owner, invoices overstate the volume or price of marine fuel, and the same fuel is re-invoiced multiple times in Suez Canal transits to mask proceeds of crime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law No. 80 of 2016: imprisonment of not less than 5 years and up to 15 years (with hard labor where aggravating circumstances exist) and a fine of EGP 100,000–1,000,000, or an amount equivalent to one-quarter of the laundered funds where higher; confiscation of the fuel cargoes, bank accounts and barges; the Suez Canal Authority and the Petroleum Authority jointly revoke the bunkering license; the ETA blocks the entity's e-invoicing and e-return accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Beneficial owners, AML compliance officers and signatories face personal criminal prosecution without limited-liability shielding; their personal assets are frozen pending investigation; the FRA instructs banks to blacklist the directors; and arrest warrants or travel bans are enforced against the controlling directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fiscal Registration and E-Filing Default: VAT, E-Invoicing and Advance Installments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register the LLC for VAT and the mandatory e-invoicing/e-receipts system, failure to file Form No. 10 and the quarterly advance installments, non-submission of Form No. 63 TP declaration, or non-appointment of a tax agent for the non-resident PE.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Lump-sum late-filing penalties of EGP 5,000–20,000 per return, plus monthly 2% corporate-tax surcharge and a parallel VAT late-filing fine of up to EGP 50,000 with 1% per-month delay interest; the ETA posts the LLC on the public default list, suspends customs release of bunker imports and blocks the electronic tax card, making port clearance for the bunkering business commercially impossible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The LLC manager and the appointed tax agent are jointly liable for penalties and for the additional tax assessed by the ETA's administrative estimation; non-payment triggers personal seizure of fees, director asset seizures, and travel bans issued by competent tax courts.
